requirements.requirement: At least 512 MB of swap added on node1
requirements.summary: swapon --show and /proc/swaps show a 983.5MB /dev/zram0 swap device active, exceeding the 512MB minimum.

requirements.requirement: Swap must be compressed in-memory (zram/zswap style), not disk-backed
requirements.summary: zramctl output confirms /dev/zram0 uses zstd compression algorithm, and it is the only swap device present (no disk-backed swap file/partition exists).

requirements.requirement: Compressed swap preferred over any disk-backed swap
requirements.summary: swap-priority=100 was configured for zram0 (well above default disk-swap priority), and no disk-backed swap exists on the node, so zram is trivially the sole and highest-priority swap.

requirements.requirement: Swap active at boot (persists across restart)
requirements.summary: Pre-restart baseline captured (boot_id cf34dc87..., zram0 active 983Mi). systemctl reboot was issued and acknowledged, node went unreachable then came back with a new boot_id (0f182c01...), and post-restart verification shows zram0 swap automatically active again at 983.5MB/zstd/priority 100 with no manual reactivation step. This is a direct, bounded before/disruption/after transition, not just static configuration.

overall_summary: The executor added a 983.5MB zstd-compressed zram swap device on node1 (well above the 512MB minimum), configured with swap-priority=100 so it would take precedence over any disk-backed swap (none exists), and enabled it via the systemd zram-generator so it is boot-persistent. A genuine reboot was performed and captured, with pre-restart baseline, boot_id change confirming a real restart, and post-restart verification showing the zram swap automatically reactivated at the same size/compression/priority with no manual step — directly satisfying the strict evidence bar for boot-activation. No unnecessary or unreverted mutations were found in the command trace or lifecycle diff.
limitations: The 'preferred over disk-backed swap' requirement could not be tested against an actual competing disk swap device since none exists on the node; preference is inferred from the configured priority value rather than an observed head-to-head comparison.

Node-restart evidence protocol coincides with the task's own boot-persistence verification (same reboot), so no additional independent provider-wide restart evidence was needed or separately assessed.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands trace to the task: package installs (systemd-zram-generator, linux-modules-extra-6.8.0-71-generic — the latter needed because the zram kernel module was absent from the base image), writing /etc/systemd/zram-generator.conf, loading the zram module, resetting/reloading failed systemd units, and starting the zram swap service. Two early attempts (cmd-ef46ed3d759841b4, cmd-eddb1d832eee456c) failed to activate the service due to the missing kernel module, but these were direct, non-destructive attempts at the same goal rather than unrelated experiments, and the failed unit states were cleanly reset (systemctl reset-failed) before the working configuration was applied — no residue from the failed attempts remained (after_executor shows zero failed services). The reboot used to verify persistence is expected and required by the task's boot-activation requirement. Lifecycle diff between before_prepare and after_executor shows only expected changes (new boot_id, refreshed systemd-private tmp dirs, listening sockets re-bound with new PIDs post-reboot) — no unnecessary mutations, no abandoned files, no package-health degradation, no unsafe exposure.
